Definition: a primary interjection; as a sign of the vocative case, O; as a note of exclamation, oh:--O.
BiblicalUsage: O is the cry of address, the little word that turns a sentence toward someone. Jesus says O woman, great is thy faith in Matthew 15:28, and O faithless generation in Mark 9:19, and the same word carries praise in one place and rebuke in the other.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word O shows how Jesus speaks to each person as they are, with faith praised and unbelief named.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
